Jordan —

Thanks, and great meeting earlier. Attaching a concise MAP draft and our unit-econ worksheet (spreadsheet stub attached as aciri_map_v1.xlsx). High level plan below — I'll follow up with a runbook and a short ops playbook that highlights prefix caching and batching tradeoffs.

Proposed MAP (summary):
- Week 1 (this week): Share MAP + baseline unit-econ (tokens/session, tokens/$, latency targets) — owner: Hannah (done: draft attached)
- Week 2: Run eval with 2k sample sessions; capture tokens/session distribution + KV hit rates — owner: Aciri/Redwood ops joint
- Week 3: Run batching/caching sensitivity sims (we provide traffic scripts) — owner: Redwood engineering (Ben/Karthik)
- Week 4: Finalize preferred config and sign PO; procurement readiness review — owner: Aciri procurement + Redwood sales

Key assumptions I put in the workbook:
- Baseline LLM model: rwd-7b-ql - 8-bit quantized; tokens/sec and per-token price line item included.
- Avg tokens/session (initial eval): 210 tokens.
- Prefix reuse expectation: 25% KV cache hit in early eval; we model up to 70% in production for high reuse prompts.
- Batching: two modes modeled — conservative (max latency 150ms added, batch size 4) and aggressive (latency impact up to 300ms, batch size 16) — both appear in the sensitivity tab.

A couple of asks from our side to make sims meaningful:
1) Share a small representative prompt set (10–50 scripts) and expected session length distribution.
2) Confirm peak QPS target and acceptable p95 latency.
3) A Procurement point of contact for the PO checklist.

Attachments: aciri_map_v1.xlsx (MAP + unit-econ workbook, stub). Also linking the drive copy: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1AciriMAPv1

If OK, Ben can run an ops primer for your infra team Wednesday afternoon.

—

Adding some technical notes we should surface in the MAP and workbook so procurement and infra teams understand tradeoffs:

- Cache model: we measure KV cache hit as percent of generations where the prefix tokens are satisfied from KV; show tokens saved as (avg_prefix_len * hit_rate). Include both absolute token savings and % cost reduction.

- Batching behavior: batching reduces compute per-token overhead but increases tail latency. In our sim sheet include: tokens/second throughput delta, per-token compute cost delta, and p95 latency for batch sizes [1,4,8,16].

- Warm-up & prefetch: for workloads with session-level reuse, prefetching the KV for top-3 prompts reduces cold-start token spend by ~30% in our past pilots. We'll add a prefetch scenario tab.

- Edge cases: bursts where QPS exceeds pool capacity — include fallback to rwd-3b (cheaper but lower perf) and show cost impact.

Attachments: sample-batching-ops.txt (run commands and expected metrics), redwood_unit_econ_notes.pdf (one-pager).

I can run the Week 3 sims; need a small sample corpus and a peek at the real session-length histogram — Jordan, can procurement share that with Hannah?

-Ben
